subject: Obtaining provisional ability estimates for a linear test

messages.author: 855dfb1ffdcf3061
messages.subject: Obtaining provisional ability estimates for a linear test
parts:
Hi everyone,

Does anyone know how can I obtain provisional ability estimates for an examinee (like the "thetas_history" output from mirCAT package) after each administered item, but for linear non-adaptive  test?

I tried to provide item parameters and full responses matrix to mirtCAT function. But the CAT algorithm adjusted and changed item administration order based on item selection rules. Does anyone know if there is an existing R package that can do this?

Thank you very much!

Best,
Siyu

messages.author: 14fdf905a5a9dcf7
messages.subject: Re: Obtaining provisional ability estimates for a linear test
parts:
Here is a quick prototype using the irtoys package and a for loop.

#########################################################
require(irtoys)

# Item parameter matrix (disc,diff,guessing)

ipar     <- matrix(NA,nrow=30,ncol=3)
ipar[,1] <- rlnorm(30,0,1) # Item discrimination
ipar[,2] <- rnorm(30,0,1)  # item difficulty
ipar[,3] <- 0              # guessing
             
# Generate a response pattern for theta = -0.5

pattern <- sim(ip = ipar, x = -.5)

# Use a for loop to estimate theta after every item (start at item 2)

th_prov <- c()

for(i in 2:length(resp)){

 th_prov[i] <- mlebme(resp = pattern[1:i],
                      ip   = ipar[1:i,],
                      method = 'ML')
}

th_prov

messages.author: 855dfb1ffdcf3061
messages.subject: Re: Obtaining provisional ability estimates for a linear test
parts:
Hello everyone,

I actually find that mirtCAT package can achieve it by adjusting some input arguments. Here is the example provided by the paper, "Generating Adaptive and Non-Adaptive Test
Interfaces for Multidimensional Item Response Theory Applications". I made some small edits:

## Define population parameters
a <- c(1, 1.2, 0.9, 0.8, 1.1, 1.2, 0.8, 0.7, 0.5, 1)
d <- c(-1, 1.5, 0, 0.5, -0.5, -1, 0, 0.1, 1.1, -0.2)
g <- rep(0.2, 10)
pars <- data.frame(a1 = a, d = d, g = g)
lc <- matrix(2)

## Generate mirt_object for CAT session
mirt_object <- generate.mirt_object(pars, itemtype = "3PL", latent_covariance = lc)
coef(mirt_object, simplify = TRUE)

## generate random response pattern
set.seed(1)
pattern <- generate_pattern(mirt_object, Theta = 1)
pattern

result <- mirtCAT(mo = mirt_object, local_pattern = pattern, start_item = 1, criteria = "seq")
result
